name: Meknes and Volubilis
tagline: A quiet imperial city of monumental gates and a sultan's stables, and the best-preserved Roman ruins in Morocco, in an olive-covered plain.
highlight: The mosaics of Volubilis, still in place, with the Roman arch and the Zerhoun hills behind.
shortDescription: A UNESCO-listed imperial city built by Sultan Moulay Ismail, with vast gates and granaries, plus the Roman site of Volubilis and the holy town of Moulay Idriss nearby.
metaDescription: A Meknes and Volubilis travel guide: Bab Mansour, Moulay Ismail's mausoleum, Heri es-Souani, the Roman mosaics of Volubilis, Moulay Idriss, day trips from Fes, and a two-day plan.
knownFor: Bab Mansour, Moulay Ismail's imperial city, Roman Volubilis
goodFor: History, Roman ruins, quiet exploration, a day trip from Fes

intro: Meknes was a modest city until the second half of the 17th century, when Sultan Moulay Ismail (r. 1672–1727) made it his capital. Over 55 years he built miles of walls, monumental gates, palaces, granaries and stables, which turned Meknes into one of Morocco's four imperial cities. UNESCO inscribed the historic city in 1996.

It is a quieter, less touristy alternative to Fes or Marrakech, with a friendly medina and a relaxed pace. The great gate of Bab Mansour, completed in 1732, is one of the finest in Morocco, and the sultan's mausoleum is one of the few in the country that non-Muslims can enter.

About 30 km north lie the ruins of Volubilis, a Roman town in the province of Mauretania Tingitana, inscribed by UNESCO in 1997. It flourished from the 1st to 3rd centuries AD on the olive and grain trade, and its mosaics, capitol and triumphal arch remain in a landscape of rolling fields. Nearby, Moulay Idriss is a hillside pilgrimage town holding the tomb of the founder of Morocco's first Islamic dynasty.

whyVisit.intro: Meknes and Volubilis together make one of the best day or two-day excursions in Morocco.

points.title: Roman Morocco
points.text: Volubilis is the best-preserved Roman site in the country, with mosaics still in their original position.

points.title: Imperial monumental architecture
points.text: Bab Mansour, the Heri es-Souani granaries and the walls show the ambitions of Moulay Ismail.

points.title: Fewer crowds
points.text: A calmer medina than Fes or Marrakech, with less hassle.

points.title: A holy hill town
points.text: Moulay Idriss stacks white houses on two hills, and is a pleasant place for lunch.

points.title: A base near Fes
points.text: Meknes is only an hour from Fes, and a good stop between Fes and Rabat.

attractionsIntro: Give Meknes a morning and Volubilis an afternoon, or stay overnight and take it slowly.

attractions.name: Bab Mansour

image.alt: The ornate green-and-white tiled Bab Mansour gate in Meknes

attractions.text: The great ceremonial gate, finished in 1732, decorated with zellige tile and marble columns, some taken from Volubilis.
attractions.tip: Photograph it in the late afternoon.

attractions.name: The Mausoleum of Moulay Ismail
attractions.text: The tomb of the sultan, a series of elegant courtyards with zellige, carved plaster and a fountain. It is open to non-Muslims, unusual in Morocco.
attractions.tip: Dress modestly and remove your shoes as requested.

attractions.name: Heri es-Souani
attractions.text: The massive granaries and former stables of the sultan, with rows of great arches in a vast space, built to house grain and horses.
attractions.tip: Combine with the neighbouring water tank.

attractions.name: Place el-Hedim and the medina
attractions.text: A large square facing Bab Mansour, with cafés and snake charmers, leading into the medina and its craft stalls.
attractions.tip: The medina is easy to explore alone.

attractions.name: Bou Inania Madrasa, Meknes
attractions.text: A 14th-century Marinid college with decorated courtyards, quieter than the one in Fes.

thingsToDoIntro: This is a place for history, and for wandering.

thingsToDo.title: Explore the Roman ruins at Volubilis
thingsToDo.text: Walk the paved main street, the basilica and the capitol, and see the mosaics, including the Labours of Hercules and Diana bathing.
thingsToDo.tip: Go in the morning, and hire a guide at the entrance.

thingsToDo.title: Visit Moulay Idriss
thingsToDo.text: A hilltop town holding the tomb of Idris I, the founder of Morocco's first Islamic dynasty. It is a pilgrimage site.
thingsToDo.tip: Non-Muslims cannot enter the shrine, but the town has views.

thingsToDo.title: Walk the imperial city
thingsToDo.text: Follow the walls and gates from Bab Mansour to the mausoleum.
thingsToDo.tip: Go early to avoid the heat.

thingsToDo.title: Taste local wine
thingsToDo.text: The Meknes region is Morocco's main wine-growing area, with vineyards and tastings.
thingsToDo.tip: Ask your hotel about tasting visits.

thingsToDo.title: Shop in the medina
thingsToDo.text: Damascene metalwork, ceramics and textiles, in a calm setting.
thingsToDo.tip: Prices are often lower than in Fes.

thingsToDo.title: Combine with Fes
thingsToDo.text: Use Meknes as a day trip from Fes or a stop on the way between Rabat and Fes.

foodIntro: Meknes is known for its olives and fruit, and its food is simple, Fassi-influenced Moroccan cooking.

foods.name: Olives
foods.text: The region is one of Morocco's big olive producers, and olives and oil are sold in the market.

foods.name: Local wine
foods.text: Red and rosé wines, from vineyards near Meknes.

accommodation.intro: Stay in the medina or the new town, and consider a night near Volubilis.

areas.name: The medina
areas.text: Riads and guesthouses near Place el-Hedim.

areas.name: Near Volubilis
areas.text: Guesthouses in the countryside or in Moulay Idriss.

gettingThere.intro: Meknes lies about 60 km west of Fes, on the main train line.

options.text: About 45 minutes to 1 hour from Fes and about 2 hours from Rabat.
options.detail: Meknes El Amir Abdelkader is the main station.

options.text: About 30 minutes from Meknes. Taxis often include Moulay Idriss.
options.detail: Agree the price and the waiting time.

options.text: Day trips from Fes cover Meknes, Volubilis and Moulay Idriss.

gettingAround.intro: The medina is on foot, and you need a taxi for Volubilis.

options.text: The medina and Place el-Hedim are walkable.
Serve the imperial city and the new town.
Shared or chartered to Volubilis and Moulay Idriss.

bestTime.headline: March–May and September–November
bestTime.summary: Meknes has hot summers and cool, wet winters. Spring and autumn are best for Volubilis, which has little shade.

seasons.text: Hot, and the Roman site has little shade.

itinerary.title: Two days in Meknes and Volubilis
itinerary.intro: The imperial city and the Roman ruins, with a stop at Moulay Idriss.

days.title: Imperial Meknes
days.morning: Bab Mansour and the Mausoleum of Moulay Ismail.

tipsIntro: A few tips help you plan the visit.
tips: Go to Volubilis in the morning, when it is cooler.
Hire a guide at the Volubilis entrance for the mosaics.
Bring a hat, sunscreen and water for the ruins.
Combine with Fes by train, or stay in Meknes.
Agree taxi fares and waiting time in advance.

faq.a: Yes, for its imperial monuments and quiet medina, and as a base for Volubilis. It is less touristy than Fes.

faq.q: How long do you need for Volubilis?
faq.a: About two hours, with a guide.

faq.q: Can I do Meknes and Volubilis as a day trip from Fes?
faq.a: Yes. It is an easy and popular day trip, by train and taxi or private driver.

faq.q: Can non-Muslims enter the mausoleum of Moulay Ismail?
faq.a: Yes, it is one of the few in Morocco open to non-Muslims.
A holy hill town that holds the tomb of Idris I, Morocco's first Islamic ruler.
